title: BlackTech_PLEAD_Backdoor_Investigation_813
description: Investigate and respond to an incident involving the BlackTech PLEAD backdoor malware.

levels.title: Introduction
levels.content: The organization has detected unusual network activity potentially related to the BlackTech threat group. Your task is to investigate and respond to this incident involving the PLEAD backdoor malware.

levels.title: Get Access
levels.cloud_content: You have SSH access to the target host (192.168.50.5) with the following credentials: Username: cyrano, Password: cyrano. Enter 'start' to begin the investigation.
levels.local_content: You have SSH access to the target host (192.168.50.5) with the following credentials: Username: cyrano, Password: cyrano. Enter 'start' to begin the investigation

levels.title: Investigate Suspicious Network Connections
levels.content: While monitoring network traffic, you've noticed unusual outbound connections from the target host. Investigate these connections to identify any suspicious activity. The suspicious port being used for command and control communication is likely to be found using network monitoring tools. Submit the suspicious port number as your answer.
levels.solution: Check active network connections and review system logs for unusual outbound traffic patterns. The suspicious port being used for command and control communication is 4444.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Check active network connections and review system logs for unusual outbound traffic patterns.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Look for unusual ports that are open and actively being used for communication.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: Use the command 'netstat -tuln' to list all active network connections.

levels.title: Analyze Persistence Mechanism
levels.content: Now that you've identified suspicious network activity, determine how the malicious process maintains persistence on the system. The persistence mechanism is likely to be found in system startup configurations or scheduled tasks. Submit the service name as your answer.
levels.solution: Examine system startup configurations and scheduled tasks that might be responsible for maintaining the malicious process. The persistence mechanism used by the malicious service is the systemd service payload-transfer.service.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Examine system startup configurations and scheduled tasks that might be responsible for maintaining the malicious process.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Look for any unusual services or cron jobs that might be responsible for starting the malicious process.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: Use the command 'systemctl list-units --type=service' to list all active services.

levels.title: Investigate Lateral Movement
levels.content: Examine evidence of potential lateral movement from the target host to other systems in the network. The script used for lateral movement is likely to be found in system directories. Submit the script path as your answer.
levels.solution: Review logs and system artifacts that might indicate file transfers or remote execution to other hosts. The service or mechanism used for lateral movement is the rsync-based payload-transfer.sh script.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Review logs and system artifacts that might indicate file transfers or remote execution to other hosts.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Look for any scripts or binaries that might be responsible for transferring files or executing commands on remote hosts.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: Use the command 'find / -name "*.sh" 2>/dev/null' to search for all shell scripts on the system.
